output.summary: The group's roughly 17.6-minute ticket time outside Riverside matches the board-accepted cost of the 2024 made-to-order menu (E4, E5), and the 12-minute benchmark excludes scratch kitchens (E3), so group-wide inefficiency is contradicted. Riverside's rise follows the August departure of its saute/pasta cook and the unfilled line position, with the station-level timings and staffing records pointing that way (E10, E11, E12). Why Marcus Delgado left is disputed and unresolved (E13, E14, E15). The repeat-visit rise coincides with a change in measurement method and a rewards launch (E7), so it is association only. Moving all kitchens to par-cooked product risks quality (E9), and a ticket-time bonus invites bumping (E18). The best next step is restoring Riverside's line position, which does not depend on the disputed explanation.
